Aria: Noticed a subtle parity/DX bug when bridging suspend token refresh into our Kotlin SDK sample app on Android 14. UI hitch + duplicate refreshes under slow networks.
Ben: Can you paste the minimal problematic pattern?
Aria: Sure. We used a suspend TokenProvider and bridged it with runBlocking inside an Interceptor: 
```
class BridgeInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val token = runBlocking { tokenProvider.getValidToken() }
    return chain.proceed(chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $token").build())
  }
}
```
Keiko: Two immediate issues: (1) runBlocking can end up using Main if tokenProvider does withContext(Main) anywhere; (2) concurrent callers generate thundering refreshes unless you single-flight them.
Marco: Also note OkHttp's RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor can replay calls, and our SDK-level retry wrapper can re-enqueue too — that combination caused repeated refresh attempts hitting our auth server rate limits in my repro.
Aria: Repro steps I used: install sampleapp -> set network to 2G throttling -> login with expiring token -> hit protected endpoint -> observe ~600-1200ms UI jank + repeated refresh logs and occasional 429s.
Ben: Quick fixes: (A) never call suspend code from interceptors via runBlocking; prefer a synchronous cache with background refresh or a single-flight suspend helper used by the network thread only. (B) if you must block, force refresh onto IO: `runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO) { ... }` (but still not ideal).
Keiko: I added a tiny single-flight helper to the sample: AtomicReference<CompletableDeferred<String>?> + doRefresh() on Dispatchers.IO and awaiting callers subscribe to the same CompletableDeferred. That eliminated duplicate refreshes in my test.
Marco: For parity we should update Java sample to show blocking refresh + explicit Executor so behavior is clear, and Kotlin sample to show single-flight suspend helper. Also document the cross-layer hazards: OkHttp replay + SDK retries + auth refresh.
CI-Bot: CI: flaky integration test https://ci/internal/28455 observed on emulator api-34 with reproducer attached.
Aria: I'll open a PR with sampleapp changes: single-flight helper, comment about Dispatchers, and a unit test that simulates interceptor re-entry and CallTimeout cancel interplay. PR #1501 incoming.
Ben: Add doc blurb under "Android integration": "Do not call suspend refresh via runBlocking from interceptors/authenticators. Use sync fast-path + single-flight refresh or ensure refresh runs on IO and propagates cancellation to the underlying OkHttp Call."
Keiko: Also add a small test that asserts no connection leaks when cancelling during refresh by checking connection pool size. I can add that.
Aria: Thanks folks — will attach repro gist and sample logs in the PR. :thumbsup:
